text.title: pnpm-package-management Core Rules
text.summary: Seven testable rules for a reproducible pnpm setup, plus the run and skip leaves.

rule.statement: Pin the pnpm version in root package.json `packageManager` field and activate via `corepack enable`.
rule.rationale: Corepack runs the exact version on every dev machine + CI, eliminating "works on my laptop" lockfile drift.

rule.statement: Keep `shamefully-hoist=false` (default). Fix phantom-dep issues via `.pnpmfile.cjs` `readPackage` hook or by declaring the missing direct dependency — never by hoisting. The one allowed escape is `node-linker=hoisted`, and only with an inline comment naming the native add-on and linking the upstream issue.
rule.rationale: Hoisting hides bugs and creates downstream version conflicts; readPackage adds the missing dep declaratively. The narrow `node-linker=hoisted` exception exists because a handful of native add-ons genuinely cannot resolve under the isolated layout — writing down which one, with a link, is what stops the exception spreading.

rule.statement: Reference internal packages with the `workspace:*` protocol; use Changesets to rewrite to real versions at publish time.
rule.rationale: workspace:* breaks at publish unless Changesets rewrites it; the combo is the only safe pattern.

rule.statement: Use `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI. Cache the pnpm store keyed by `pnpm-lock.yaml` hash.
rule.rationale: --frozen-lockfile blocks drift; store caching saves 30-60s per CI run.
Without the lockfile, every install is a fresh resolution; reproducibility lost.

rule.statement: Set `"scripts.preinstall": "npx -y only-allow pnpm"` in the root package.json so an accidental `npm install` or `yarn` fails immediately instead of writing a second lockfile.
rule.rationale: A mixed package manager produces a second lockfile and an npm-shaped `node_modules`, and the resulting install is neither reproducible nor diagnosable from the diff. The guard costs one line and fails at the earliest possible moment.

rule.statement: Land `pnpm-lock.yaml` updates in a commit separate from application code changes.
rule.rationale: A commit that mixes a lockfile diff with app changes cannot be bisected: the regression is either in the dependency bump or in the code, and the commit gives you no way to tell which.

rule.statement: packageManager pinned, lockfile committed in its own commit, shamefully-hoist off, `only-allow pnpm` preinstall guard present, CI uses frozen-lockfile, workspace:* used.
pnpm not acceptable for the project (npm/yarn mandated, or Deno).
